messages:
Alex W.: quick ask — running a residency-sampling bakeoff (time-window vs request-weighted) and the aggregated hit_rate numbers don't line up with the sampled residency exporter. suspect sampler bias. anyone seen this before?
Priya R.: which panels are you comparing? grafana or the raw prom queries?
Alex W.: grafana + the raw counters. e.g. dashboard panel shows kv.cache.hit_rate ~ 0.82 but the residency sampler reports sampled_residency_pct ~ 0.92 for the same window.
Minh T.: common pitfall: our sampler tends to oversample long-lived sessions / long-context requests, which inflates residency. the dashboard is token-weighted though.
Dana S.: can you paste the queries? might be a labeling mismatch.
Alex W.: sure — the hit rate panel uses: ```promql
sum(rate(kv_cache_hits_total[5m])) / sum(rate(kv_cache_requests_total[5m]))
```
Alex W.: sampler emits a per-session residency that we avg across samples: ```text
avg(sampled_session_residency_pct) by (model)
```
Minh T.: there's the problem — averaging per-session residencies without weighting by requests/tokens will bias toward long-sessions. try request-weighted average or compute token-weighted residency.
Jules K.: +1. also check eviction counters. if eviction events are concentrated in a few hot sessions they skew things. add eviction_age_histogram to see if we're ejecting very old fragments or churning recently-inserted ones.
Dana S.: we should also surface an eviction_reason label (e.g., memory_pressure, ttl, explicit_delete) so dashboards can break down causes.
Priya R.: actionable ask: (1) add token/request-weighted residency panel, (2) add eviction_age_histogram & eviction_reason labels, (3) run the sampling bakeoff with a reservoir sampler variant. I can add the dashboard panels — want any panel layouts?
Alex W.: nice. for the bakeoff, let's compare three samplers: naive-time-window, request-weighted reservoir, and per-session reservoir capped at N samples/session. measure bias vs ground-truth tracer snapshot.
Minh T.: I can script the tracer snapshots. will run across a 24h window including the kernel-selection perf reg from Mar 10 — curious if that reg increased evictions.
Jules K.: reminder: the Mar 10 kernel tweak reduced KV bucket size (intentional for kernel memory locality) — I saw a temporary bump in eviction_rate on canary. might explain memory growth over long contexts if fragmentation spikes.
Dana S.: for dashboards, add a heatmap: kv_residency_percentile{p="p50|p90|p99"} by (model, region). that helps teams see long-tail sessions.
Priya R.: will add panels and a new 'KV sampling bakeoff' row in infra/growth dashboard. pinning queries here for review: ```promql
// token-weighted residency
sum(rate(kv_cached_tokens_total[5m])) / sum(rate(kv_requested_tokens_total[5m]))
```
Priya R.: also adding an 'eviction-age-by-reason' table + sparklines.
Alex W.: excellent. last bit — can we expose a derived metric: kv_reuse_ratio = hits / (inserts - evictions) to surface reuse efficiency? might be noisy but useful for regression alerts.
Minh T.: like it. also track per-model kv_eviction_rate_per_1e6_tokens. helps normalize by workload.
deploy-bot: deploy: rollout of metrics/telemetry v2 completed to canary cluster (canary-3) — logs: https://deploys/reports/1735009
Jules K.: once priya lands panels we should run the bakeoff and collect a short report. assign: Priya -> dashboard, Minh -> tracer-run + bakeoff script, Alex -> sampler PR with request-weighted avg, Dana -> eviction_reason label + histogram instrument.
Priya R.: ACK, will open dashboard PR and add notes in the panel descriptions on expected bias.
Alex W.: thanks all — target to have results by EOD Friday. feel free to ping me if you need sample queries or tracer snapshots. :thumbsup:
